```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)
library(knitr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 150, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "–")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

PROC <- "data/processed"
pull_log <- fromJSON("data/pull_log.json")
UNIT <- 1000; N_INVEST <- 100; MEAN_R <- 1.35; MEAN_D <- 1.00
COND_COLORS <- c(control = "#9ca3af", treatment = "#2563eb")
COND_LABELS <- c(control = "Control (cats-vs-dogs bot)", treatment = "Treatment (Republican persona bot)")
se <- function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)

parts <- read_csv(file.path(PROC, "participants.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(across(c(started_at, completed_at, game_finished_at, starts_with("ts_")), ymd_hms),
         completed = !is.na(completed_at))
inv <- read_csv(file.path(PROC, "investments.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(R = county == "R", saved_at = ymd_hms(saved_at))
screen <- read_csv(file.path(PROC, "screenouts.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
errors <- read_csv(file.path(PROC, "client_errors.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
chats <- read_csv(file.path(PROC, "chat_messages.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
done <- parts |> filter(completed, n_investments_saved == N_INVEST)
n_by <- count(done, condition) |> deframe()
```

## Snapshot

Data pulled `r format(with_tz(ymd_hms(pull_log$pulled_at), "America/New_York"), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")` ET from MongoDB `twins-bandit-game` and the chatbot's Postgres log (Prolific study `r pull_log$prolific_study_id`; app tag `v3.0.0-bandit-pilot`).

**Design.** Democrats who pass screening chat for 5 minutes with a Republican persona bot (treatment) or a bot that debates cats vs dogs (control). They then invest a $100,000 budget in 100 clicks of $1,000. Each click goes to Riverton County (Republican-leaning) or Lakewood County (Democratic-leaning) and shows the money that came back right away. A $1,000 investment brings back $1,350 on average in Riverton and $1,000 in Lakewood, with large luck: one return's SD is 61% (Riverton) and 71% (Lakewood) of its mean. Sending every click to Riverton is best. The k-th treated and k-th control participant face the same sequence of returns. The bonus maps money back from $100,000 (expected if every click goes to Lakewood) to $135,000 (every click to Riverton) onto $0 to $1.00.

This pilot has `r nrow(done)` complete participants (`r n_by["treatment"]` treatment, `r n_by["control"]` control). Every condition comparison below is descriptive; its purpose is to check that the game works and to size the main study.

## 1. Flow, timing and data quality

```{r flow}
tibble(
  Step = c("Screened out before assignment", "Assigned", "Completed (all 100 clicks and demographics)"),
  Total = c(nrow(screen), nrow(parts), nrow(done)),
  Treatment = c(NA, sum(parts$condition == "treatment"), n_by["treatment"]),
  Control = c(NA, sum(parts$condition == "control"), n_by["control"])
) |> kable(caption = "Participant flow (counts of people).")

# Screen timestamps come from the participant's browser clock; drop people whose clock is off by more
# than 5 minutes (browser time at assignment vs the server's assignment time).
times <- done |>
  mutate(skew_min = abs(as.numeric(difftime(ts_chat_intro, started_at, units = "mins")))) |>
  filter(skew_min < 5) |>
  mutate(total_min = as.numeric(difftime(completed_at, ts_attention_math, units = "mins")),
         game_min = as.numeric(difftime(game_finished_at, ts_game, units = "mins")),
         tut_min = as.numeric(difftime(ts_game, ts_game_tutorial, units = "mins")))
```

Median time from the consent click to the end was `r fmt(median(times$total_min, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` minutes (range `r fmt(min(times$total_min, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`–`r fmt(max(times$total_min, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`); pay covers 10 minutes. Timing excludes `r nrow(done) - nrow(times)` participants whose browser clocks were off by hours. The instructions took a median of `r fmt(median(times$tut_min, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` minutes and the 100 clicks `r fmt(median(times$game_min, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` minutes.

```{r integrity}
inv_chk <- inv |> group_by(participant_id) |>
  summarise(gaps = !all(sort(n) == seq_along(n)), .groups = "drop")
tibble(
  Check = c("Completers with fewer than 100 saved clicks", "Clicks saved out of order or with gaps",
            "Clicks where the browser's money back differs from the server's",
            "Completers whose browser bonus differs from the server bonus (> 1¢)",
            "Client errors logged", "Treated participants not served the Republican bot",
            "Control participants not served the cats-vs-dogs bot"),
  Problems = c(sum(done$n_investments_saved < N_INVEST), sum(inv_chk$gaps), sum(done$n_back_mismatch),
               sum(abs(done$game_bonus - done$game_bonus_client) > 0.011, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(errors),
               sum(!parts$participant_id[parts$condition == "treatment"] %in%
                     chats$participant_id[chats$bot_prompt %in% "republican_persona"]),
               sum(!parts$participant_id[parts$condition == "control"] %in%
                     chats$participant_id[chats$bot_prompt %in% "cats_dogs"]))
) |> kable(caption = "Integrity checks (0 means clean).")
```

## 2. Learning across the game

```{r curves, fig.height = 4.8}
blocks <- inv |> filter(participant_id %in% done$participant_id) |>
  mutate(block = (n - 1) %/% 10 + 1) |>
  group_by(participant_id, condition, block) |> summarise(share_R = mean(R), .groups = "drop")
sim <- read_csv("../09_bandit_prototype/output/curves.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(ratio == 1.35, n0_med == 20, group %in% c("Control", "Ideal learner")) |>
  mutate(block = (visit - 1) %/% 10 + 1) |> group_by(group, block) |> summarise(p = mean(p_r), .groups = "drop")
blocks |> group_by(condition, block) |> summarise(m = mean(share_R), s = se(share_R), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(block, m, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line(data = sim, aes(block, p, linetype = group), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = m - s, ymax = m + s, fill = condition), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey80") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COND_COLORS, labels = COND_LABELS, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COND_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Control = "dotted", `Ideal learner` = "dashed"),
                        labels = c(Control = "Simulated Democrats (design memo)", `Ideal learner` = "Ideal learner (simulation)"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, labels = paste0(seq(1, 91, 10), "–", seq(10, 100, 10))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Clicks", y = "Share of clicks to Riverton") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))
```

*Figure 1. Share of clicks sent to Riverton in each block of 10 clicks, by condition (mean ± 1 SE across participants). Black lines come from the design simulation (`studies/09_bandit_prototype`, Riverton 1.35×, prior worth about 20 clicks): dotted, simulated Democrats who start out believing Lakewood is better; dashed, an ideal learner.*

```{r learning-summary}
pooled <- blocks |> group_by(block) |> summarise(m = mean(share_R), .groups = "drop")
better <- count(done, pilot_better_county)
```

People learned, but slowly. Across both conditions the Riverton share rose from `r scales::percent(pooled$m[1], 1)` in clicks 1–10 to `r scales::percent(pooled$m[10], 1)` in clicks 91–100; an ideal learner reaches about 90%. After the game, `r better$n[better$pilot_better_county == "Riverton"]` of `r nrow(done)` people said Riverton brought back more money per $1,000.

## 3. Treatment vs control

```{r tvc}
per <- inv |> filter(participant_id %in% done$participant_id) |>
  group_by(participant_id, condition) |>
  summarise(first_R = as.numeric(R[n == 1]), share_1_10 = mean(R[n <= 10]), share_all = mean(R),
            share_91_100 = mean(R[n > 90]), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(done, participant_id, game_bonus), by = "participant_id")
outcomes <- c(first_R = "First click to Riverton (before any feedback)", share_1_10 = "Riverton share, clicks 1–10",
              share_all = "Riverton share, all 100 clicks", share_91_100 = "Riverton share, clicks 91–100",
              game_bonus = "Bonus ($)")
tvc <- map_dfr(names(outcomes), function(o) {
  t <- per[[o]][per$condition == "treatment"]; c <- per[[o]][per$condition == "control"]
  tt <- t.test(t, c)
  sp <- sqrt(((length(t) - 1) * var(t) + (length(c) - 1) * var(c)) / (length(t) + length(c) - 2))
  tibble(Outcome = outcomes[o], `Treatment mean (SE)` = paste0(fmt(mean(t)), " (", fmt(se(t)), ")"),
         `Control mean (SE)` = paste0(fmt(mean(c)), " (", fmt(se(c)), ")"),
         `Diff (T − C)` = fmt(mean(t) - mean(c)), `95% CI` = paste0("[", fmt(tt$conf.int[1]), ", ", fmt(tt$conf.int[2]), "]"),
         p = fmt(tt$p.value), d = fmt((mean(t) - mean(c)) / sp), sd_pooled = sp)
})
tvc |> select(-sd_pooled) |> kable(caption = "Treatment minus control, one value per participant. Welch t-test CIs; Cohen's d uses the pooled SD.")
```

```{r tvc-text}
d_all <- tvc$d[tvc$Outcome == outcomes["share_all"]]
diff_all <- as.numeric(tvc$`Diff (T − C)`[tvc$Outcome == outcomes["share_all"]])
```

Treated participants sent fewer clicks to Riverton than control participants: `r scales::percent(abs(diff_all), 1)` fewer over all 100 clicks (d = `r d_all`), the opposite of the hypothesis. The first click, made before any feedback, barely differs. With `r min(n_by)` people in the smaller condition, a two-sided t-test has 80% power only for d ≥ `r fmt(pwr_d <- power.t.test(n = min(n_by), power = 0.8)$delta, 2)`, so the direction is a hint at most.

```{r individual, fig.height = 3.6}
per |> mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("control", "treatment"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(share_all, condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.12, width = 0, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, colour = "black", geom = "pointrange") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COND_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = COND_LABELS) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Share of all 100 clicks to Riverton", y = NULL)
```

*Figure 2. Each dot is one participant's share of clicks to Riverton; black points are condition means ± 1 SE.*

## 4. Response to feedback

```{r feedback}
fb <- inv |> filter(participant_id %in% done$participant_id) |> arrange(participant_id, n) |>
  group_by(participant_id) |>
  mutate(next_county = lead(county), good = back >= UNIT) |> ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(next_county)) |>
  mutate(stay = next_county == county)
fb_tab <- fb |> group_by(participant_id, condition, county, good) |> summarise(stay = mean(stay), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(condition, County = if_else(county == "R", "Riverton", "Lakewood"),
           `Last return` = if_else(good, "$1,000 or more", "under $1,000")) |>
  summarise(`P(stay), mean (SE)` = paste0(fmt(mean(stay)), " (", fmt(se(stay)), ")"), People = n(), .groups = "drop")
kable(fb_tab, caption = "Probability of clicking the same county again after a good (≥ $1,000) or bad (< $1,000) return; mean across participants.")
```

People respond to feedback: they stay with a county more often after a good return than after a bad one, in both counties and both conditions. Table 4 is the raw material for the learning model in the main study (separate learning rates for good and bad news from each county).

## 6. Chat content

```{r chats}
user_chats <- chats |> filter(!is_system_prompt) |> inner_join(select(done, participant_id, condition), by = "participant_id")
chat_sum <- user_chats |>
  mutate(text = str_to_lower(paste(coalesce(message, ""), coalesce(response, ""))),
         user_words = str_count(coalesce(message, ""), "\\S+")) |>
  group_by(participant_id, condition) |>
  summarise(msgs = n(), user_words = sum(user_words),
            solar = any(str_detect(text, "solar|panel")), energy = any(str_detect(text, "energy|electric|climate|environment")),
            .groups = "drop")
chat_sum |> group_by(Condition = condition) |>
  summarise(People = n(), `Messages, mean` = fmt(mean(msgs), 1), `Words typed, mean` = fmt(mean(user_words), 0),
            `Mentioned solar or panels` = sum(solar), `Mentioned energy, climate or environment` = sum(energy)) |>
  kable(caption = "Chat engagement and topics (participant messages and bot replies).")
```

The treatment chat rarely reaches the product: only `r sum(chat_sum$solar[chat_sum$condition == "treatment"])` of `r sum(chat_sum$condition == "treatment")` treated participants' chats mention solar or panels. The persona prompt is a generic Republican consumer, and nothing in the flow points the conversation at solar.

## 7. Sizing the main study

```{r power}
sd_all <- tvc$sd_pooled[tvc$Outcome == outcomes["share_all"]]
sd_10 <- tvc$sd_pooled[tvc$Outcome == outcomes["share_1_10"]]
n_for <- function(d) ceiling(power.t.test(delta = d, power = 0.8)$n)
tibble(`Effect (Cohen's d)` = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5)) |>
  mutate(`People per condition (80% power, two-sided α = .05)` = map_int(`Effect (Cohen's d)`, n_for),
         `Same effect in Riverton share, all clicks (points)` = round(100 * `Effect (Cohen's d)` * sd_all, 1),
         `Same effect in Riverton share, clicks 1–10 (points)` = round(100 * `Effect (Cohen's d)` * sd_10, 1)) |>
  kable(caption = "Sample size per condition by effect size, with each d translated into percentage points of Riverton share using this pilot's pooled SDs.")
```

The pooled SD of the all-clicks Riverton share is `r fmt(100 * sd_all, 0)` points, so a 10-point treatment effect is d ≈ `r fmt(0.10 / sd_all, 2)` and needs about `r n_for(0.10 / sd_all)` people per condition.
